title: ImageNet-trained CNNs are not biased towards texture: Revisiting feature re

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The caption states: 'It includes results for models trained from scratch as well as a class-wise analysis for ImageNet, which confirms that the global reliance patterns are consistent across categories.' The actual figure shows only domain-averaged feature suppression curves for CV, MI, and RS, with no such from-scratch model results or class-wise analysis visible. The caption describes content not present in the figure.

For the shape-suppressing transformations (Patch Shuffle and Patch Rotation), the texture preservation metrics (LV↑ and HFE↑) are reported as exactly 1.000, implying no change in local variance or high-frequency energy. Shuffling or rotating image patches creates discontinuities at patch boundaries that alter both local variance and high-frequency content; a perfect score of 1.000 across 800 images is extremely implausible and suggests the metrics were not correctly computed or that the validation is unreliable.
Neither reference [11] (Landau et al.) nor [44] (Miller, WordNet) is cited anywhere in the main text. All references should be cited; uncited references are a standard citation error.

In Section 5.1 the texture suppression experiment uses bilateral filtering with d=12, σ_color=170, σ_space=75. The quantitative validation in Table 2 (Param ID A) used d=11, σ_color=170, σ_space=75. The parameters do not match, so the validation does not directly apply to the experiment’s suppression.

The text states: 'color suppression induces a substantial decline in classification accuracy for most datasets ... except in ChestMNIST, which contains only grayscale images.' However, Figure 4 (middle row) shows only five MedMNIST-v2 datasets (BloodMNIST, BreastMNIST, DermaMNIST, OCTMNIST, PathMNIST) and does not include ChestMNIST. Referencing a dataset not shown in the corresponding figure creates a mismatch.
